cases.prompt: Photorealistic digital illustration of a futuristic cyberpunk city at night, viewed from street level along a broad avenue after heavy rain. The wet black asphalt fills the foreground, reflecting long bands of cyan, magenta, violet, and acid-red neon light in broken ripples around shallow puddles. A narrow stream of runoff crosses the bottom edge beside a grated drain clogged with scraps of paper and metallic debris. In the center, a low autonomous taxi with a dark glass canopy drives toward the viewer, its angular body edged by red warning lights and illuminated by blue underbody strips. Water sprays behind its wheels, while two smaller vehicles recede into the distance as elongated silhouettes with glowing tail lamps. On both sides, dense towers rise beyond stacked balconies, exposed pipes, ventilation ducts, suspended cables, and crowded storefronts. Vertical neon signs project over the sidewalks: a cyan sign on the left reads "NIGHT MARKET", a magenta sign above it reads "SYNTHETIC DISTRICT", and a red sign on the right reads "OPEN 24 HOURS". Smaller panels display abstract symbols and illegible fine print. Elevated pedestrian bridges cross between buildings overhead, carrying clusters of dark human silhouettes beneath transparent umbrellas. Near the left curb, a compact food stall glows turquoise under a striped awning, with steam rising from a metal vent and catching pink light. On the right, a lone figure in a long black hooded coat stands beneath a transparent umbrella, facing the traffic; the coat’s reflective seams trace electric-blue highlights across the shoulders. Tall holographic advertisements float above the intersection, including a rotating wireframe face surrounded by pulsing geometric graphics. In the background, skyscrapers merge into a dark canyon of illuminated windows, rooftop antennas, and luminous skybridges. Low clouds obscure the upper towers, while mist and rain scatter the neon into colored halos around the highest signs.
cases.notes: Replaces flux1_dev_t2i_1024 and flux2_dev_t2i_1024 (retired 2026-10-15); their published results stay in the reports. Base checkpoint, not the step-distilled black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein: a distilled, reduced-step model is a lossy substitute under this repo's policy. 50 steps and CFG 3.5 are the Base settings sglang's FLUX.3 cookbook validated at 1024x1024 (sglang#44418); the seed is the retired FLUX rows'. The prompt is the retired rows' short request ("A futuristic cyberpunk city at night, neon lights reflecting on wet streets") expanded once by BFL's prompt upsampler, because the model card says FLUX.3 is not meant to run on a short prompt: black-forest-labs/flux-3-image-klein-pup rev 3f3edb52, served by sglang with --enable-deterministic-inference --disable-radix-cache through the flux3-klein-pup enhancer protocol (sglang PR, 2026-10-16), caption md5 b0e44fd9c061; reruns reproduce it exactly. The caption is frozen here so every framework encodes the same 303 words; the upsampler itself is not timed. The repo is gated (auto-approved request plus the flux-kommunity-license); the account whose HF_TOKEN the run uses must have accepted it. ComfyUI serves it on master (official v0.41 templates); vLLM-Omni and TensorRT-LLM have open PRs (2026-10-16). Measured on 2xH200 2026-10-16 with this caption: sglang 4.035 s, ComfyUI 5.364 s (vLLM-Omni pre-merge 4.534 s); other hardware VALIDATION PENDING.

cases.label: Qwen-Image-2.1 T2I 1024
cases.prompt: A warehouse robot folds a blue cloth on a clean workbench.
cases.notes: ONE GPU on purpose: this case exists to compare the same model across a datacenter/consumer hardware range (H200, B200, RTX 5090, RTX 4090), and one GPU is the only configuration all four can run. The cookbook also verifies b200-2-tp and b200-2-ulysses; keep those behind an explicit --case-ids rerun rather than splitting this row. output_format=png is REQUIRED, not a preference: this checkpoint emits RGBA and the default JPEG encoder raises `cannot write mode RGBA as JPEG`, which reaches the client as a bare HTTP 500. 40 steps is the checkpoint default per the cookbook; guidance_scale 1.0 means no CFG, so do not add a CFG-parallel flag here. On torch.compile: unlike qwen_image_2512, `--performance-mode speed` does NOT need to be paired with `--enable-torch-compile false` here. The runtime refuses compile for this model on its own -- the B200 server log says `torch.compile disabled for this model` and resolves `enable_torch_compile: false` -- so every row in this case is eager, which is what the best-lossless policy wants anyway. Re-check this if upstream enables compile for Qwen-Image-2.1; the profiles would then need the explicit flag or a measured exception. MULTI-GPU, measured 2026-09-21 on one 2xB200 box (sglang 176dbcb8), probe form, median of 3 after warmup, resident + --attention-backend fa throughout so parallelism is the only variable. This workload (no CFG): 1 GPU 2.497s -> --tp-size 2 1.626s (1.54x, 26.6 GB/card) -> --ulysses-degree 2 1.703s (1.47x, 37.4 GB/card); TP also shards the weights where Ulysses replicates them. On a true-CFG workload (true_cfg_scale 4.0 + the standard negative prompt, two DiT forwards per step): 1 GPU 4.827s -> --tp-size 2 3.106s (1.55x) -> --cfg-parallel-size 2 2.601s (1.86x), i.e. CFG-parallel beats TP by 1.19x and is near-linear, matching this repo's Qwen-Image-2512 finding that CFG parallelism is the reliable Qwen multi-GPU speedup and TP is not the latency path. CFG-parallel cannot be measured on THIS case: with guidance_scale 1.0 there is one branch, rank 1 has no work, and the runtime rejects the request. Multi-GPU stays behind an explicit --case-ids rerun per the one-representative-case rule; the numbers live in reports/qwen-image-21-hardware-sweep-20260921/.

rtx5090-1gpu-encoder-layerwise-offload.description: RTX 5090 32GB: DiT and VAE resident, Qwen3-VL encoder streamed layerwise.
rtx5090-1gpu-encoder-layerwise-offload.serve_args: --model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --performance-mode manual --component-residency dit=resident text_encoder=layerwise-offload vae=resident --warmup-resolutions 1024x1024
rtx5090-1gpu-encoder-layerwise-offload.policy_exception: Offload is not a tuning choice on this card, it is the only way the model runs: a 30.9 GiB checkpoint on 32 GB. The cookbook's picker DISABLES resident placement on RTX 5090 outright ('the full resident pipeline exceeds one consumer GPU's memory. Select CPU offload.'), so there is no resident arm to compare against. This recipe offloads the least it can: only the Qwen3-VL encoder streams, the DiT and VAE stay resident. Measured 2026-09-21 on a 1x RTX 5090 devbox at p50 14.082s using 17.0 GB steady.
rtx5090-1gpu-encoder-layerwise-offload.notes: NOT the cookbook's RTX 5090 recipe -- this is the cookbook's RTX 4090 recipe, measured here to be substantially faster on the 5090 as well. A/B on ONE box (bench-5090-qi21, sglang 6ad78f22, same card, same Torch SDPA, same 40 steps / seed 42 / CFG 1 / PNG; only component placement differs, which does not change numerics): cookbook `--dit-layerwise-offload true` p50 19.946s [19.97, 19.95, 19.95], 0.4674 s/step, 19.3 GB steady, vs this recipe p50 14.082s [14.14, 14.08, 14.08], 0.3166 s/step, 17.0 GB steady. 1.42x faster on LESS steady memory, with 0.1% scatter on each arm and no overlap between them. Cause: the cookbook's 5090 branch streams the DiT itself through every one of the 40 steps, while this one keeps the DiT on the card and streams only the encoder, which runs once per request. Peak during load is higher (24.9 GB vs 19.3 GB) and still well inside 32 GB. Upstream's picker gates the DiT-resident branch on `hw === 'rtx4090'`; on this evidence it should cover the RTX 5090 too -- see `consumer-dit-layerwise-offload-reference` for the arm this replaced.

Outside it the picker degrades to `--dit-layerwise-offload true --text-encoder-cpu-offload true`, which is a different measurement -- do not substitute one for the other. VALIDATED 2026-09-21 on a 1x RTX 4090 devbox (sglang 6ad78f22): p50 19.309s over 3 repeats after warmup [19.20, 19.31, 19.32], 0.4353 s/step x 40 = 17.41s of the 19.31s, 20.6 GB after load settling to 16.6 GB steady out of 24 GB. Note the 24 GB card lands FASTER than the 32 GB RTX 5090 (19.309s vs 19.946s) and on less memory, because this recipe keeps the DiT on the card and streams only the encoder, while the 5090 recipe streams the DiT itself every step.

h200-1gpu-fa3.description: H200: upstream's general config unchanged (FA3 is a Hopper kernel).
h200-1gpu-fa3.notes: H200 runs upstream's general config unchanged (FA3 is a Hopper kernel). MEASURED 2026-09-21 on a 1x H200 devbox, LightX2V main 4d709c43 inside upstream's own image (lightx2v/lightx2v:26062001-cu130, torch 2.11.0+cu130, base.sh confirming BF16 with no sensitive-layer override). NO RESOLVABLE SPEED DIFFERENCE against sglang: three interleaved ABAB rounds of 5 requests each, on the SAME physical node (gpu1-10-220-51-55) with the neighbouring devbox's GPU verified idle before each measurement, gave paired diffs of -0.2%, +9.6%, -0.4% -- mixed sign, so nothing to claim. sglang's 15 samples span 4.51-4.57s; LightX2V's 15 are ten at ~4.50 and five at ~5.00. The bimodality is NOT compute: its server-side `RUN pipeline` is 4.443-4.477s across eight requests (0.8% spread). Every LightX2V client latency lands within 0.010s of a 0.5s multiple while its server times do not, i.e. the sync endpoint releases on a ~0.5s tick and the H200's compute sits on the 4.5s boundary. On a 4.5s workload that tick is 11%, coarser than the ~2% being compared, so the client metric cannot separate these two frameworks on this model -- use the server-side numbers (sglang 4.342s) as the diagnostic.

Every other LightX2V case in this matrix runs flash_attn2 on Blackwell (their blackwell-fa2 profiles), the same exact-softmax class, so this follows that pattern and changes nothing else (no offload, no quantization, fused kernels as upstream). First measured on B200 in the 2026-09-25 round; the venv holds torch 2.11.0 as LightX2V's own image does, because flash-attn 2.8.3 does not compile against torch 2.14.

rtx5090-1gpu-fa2.description: RTX 5090: upstream's own lossless 5090 config -- FlashAttention2 plus text-encoder CPU offload.
rtx5090-1gpu-fa2.notes: Transcribed from configs/qwen_image_21/qwen_image_21_5090.json -- the NON-quantized 5090 config, which upstream ships alongside the FP8 ones. FA2 against sglang's Torch SDPA is a fair swap: both are exact softmax, and this repo's rule is that each framework gets its fastest kernel of the same precision class. MEASURED 2026-09-21 on a 1x RTX 5090 devbox, LightX2V main 4d709c43 inside upstream's own image (lightx2v/lightx2v:26062001-cu130-5090-fix-260921, torch 2.11.0+cu130, base.sh confirming BF16 with no sensitive-layer override): p50 14.51s, and unlike the H200 it is perfectly unimodal (seven repeats all 14.51) because its compute sits safely below the 14.5s tick boundary and pays a flat ~0.36s. Interleaved ABAB against sglang on the SAME node, 3 rounds x 5 requests: sglang 14.087 / 14.096 / 14.080 against LightX2V 14.514 / 14.513 / 14.512 -- paired diffs +2.9%, +2.9%, +3.0%, 3/3 agreeing in sign, round-to-round spread 0.1% on both sides. This one resolves (the H200 pair does not). About a third of that is the tick; server-side the gap is ~1.9% (sglang 13.879s vs 14.10-14.20s). The memory difference is the one that is not marginal: 17.0 GB steady against 30.7 GB on a 32 GB card. Output equivalence was checked rather than assumed: both return a 1024x1024 PNG at color type 6 (RGBA), LightX2V's alpha carrying real data (range 253-255). The response-size difference is the envelope, not the image -- sglang's 2.43 MB is base64 JSON around a ~1.83 MB PNG against LightX2V's 1.88 MB of raw PNG -- so there is no encode-cost asymmetry between them. INSTALL: do NOT use scripts/install_comparison_frameworks.sh for this -- it builds flash-attn 2.8.3 from source, which cannot compile against torch 2.14+cu130 (flash-attn pins -std=c++17, torch's ATen needs C++20, and 2.8.3.post1 is the newest PyPI release). Upstream's image has flash_attn, flash_attn_interface, flashinfer and sageattention prebuilt. Note also that the tag in LightX2V's README (26062001) does not exist; real tags carry a platform suffix.

default.serve_args: --model-type diffusion --warmup-mode server --enable-cfg-parallel --ulysses-degree 2 --dit-cpu-offload false --pin-cpu-memory --dit-layerwise-offload false --performance-mode speed --enable-torch-compile false
default.notes: Keep this profile updated when the best command changes for a SGLang release or commit. Policy-aligned candidate (compile on, offload off) — NOT yet validated on H100; validate (incl. OOM risk) before publishing. FOUR-GPU CELLS ON THE 2026-09-13 4xB200 RUN ARE 3-4x SLOW AND IT IS NOT SGLANG. All three 4-GPU cases (this one, cosmos3 t2v 189f, cosmos3 i2v 189f) came out 3-4x slower than the SAME case and workload on H100 (07-03, 07-30) and H200 (08-26), three runs that agree with each other inside 2%. Every framework in those cells moved together -- sglang 0.25-0.32x, vLLM-Omni 0.28-0.30x, LightX2V 0.22x -- so the earlier note here calling it a suspected sglang regression was wrong, and is retracted. Nor is it the box: every 2-GPU case in that same run is 1.7-2.6x FASTER than its H200 figure. The discriminator is GPU COUNT, not model and not framework; the original investigation missed it because every image case is 2-GPU. Already eliminated, do not repeat: model unchanged since 2025-08-09, workload identical in both artifacts, warmup scales linearly, attention backend (`fa` is WORSE than the auto-selected dynamic_cudnn_sdpa), interconnect topology (NV18 all-pairs at 53.125 GB/s), offload off with 113 GiB free, MoE boundary 0.875 with both experts resident. SETTLED: a fresh 4xB200 does NOT reproduce it. MEASURED 2026-09-18 on a fresh 4xB200 (verda-b200-fin-03-3, same node family, sglang v0.5.20, cosmos3 t2v 189f, identical workload and the same `--attention-backend fa`): 2 GPU on cards 0,1 = 58.05s; 2 GPU on cards 2,3 = 58.24s; 4 GPU = 32.34s. Four-GPU scaling is healthy (1.80x over two), and the 4-GPU figure is 1.64x faster than H200's 53.09s -- the normal Blackwell gain. bench-0912 reported 214.90s for that same cell, 6.6x the healthy number. So the hardware is fine and these three cells are ARTIFACTS OF THAT BOX, not Blackwell and not sglang -- which is also the only account consistent with vLLM-Omni and LightX2V being equally slow there. Two further hypotheses died in the same experiment: `fa` is not pathological on Blackwell (arm A pins it and is 1.9x faster than H200), and the NUMA split that puts GPU3 on a different socket costs nothing measurable (58.05 vs 58.24 across it). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18 and republished: cosmos3 t2v 214.9 -> 31.7, i2v 216.0 -> 31.9, wan22 669.4 -> 106.5, each now 1.68-1.98x faster than its H200 figure, in line with every 2-GPU cell. The two cosmos3 cells ran against Cosmos3-Nano e59a53c25 rather than the 7a312c868 the rest of the artifact records -- the shared cache resolves `main` online, so the revision could not be pinned; both cells reproduce under 0.1% across two runs and vLLM-Omni moved by the same factor, so the revision does not carry the result.

default.description: ComfyUI master, core nodes only, the model's official workflow with full-precision weights.
default.notes: Official 'Text to Video (Wan 2.2)' full-step workflow (no Lightning LoRA) with fp16 experts and UMT5 in place of fp8_scaled: two KSamplerAdvanced passes, high-noise expert then low-noise, cfg 4.0 / 3.0 as the case, shift 5.0 (sglang's 720p Wan config uses the same). The experts hand over at the half-way step -- both are 14B, so where the hand-over falls does not change the cost. Negative prompt = sglang's Wan2.2 default, encoded every request as sglang does. Two GPUs through the MultiGPU CFG Split node (ComfyUI has no sequence parallelism). Weights are the full-precision single-file checkpoints ComfyUI loads (Comfy-Org repackaging or the model's own single-file release); the official template's fp8/int8/nvfp4 defaults are swapped out because they are a different numeric class from every other row. Sampler, scheduler and shift follow the official ComfyUI workflow; steps, CFG, size, frames and seed follow the case. Compile off: TorchCompileModel together with the MultiGPU CFG Split node fails on the first request (dynamo: 'RuntimeError when making fake tensor call' in KSamplerAdvanced; ComfyUI 88ab4a06, 1xB200->2xB200, 2026-09-25). Splitting the two CFG branches over two cards roughly halves each step, which outweighs compile's measured 16-18% on FLUX.1, so the cell keeps the split and runs eager.
default.policy_exception: Compile broken with the CFG split, not a speed choice (2026-09-25, ComfyUI 88ab4a06, 1xB200->2xB200, see notes): TorchCompileModel with the MultiGPU CFG Split node fails the first request (dynamo 'RuntimeError when making fake tensor call' in KSamplerAdvanced), and the split is worth more than compile's measured 16-18% on FLUX.1.

default.description: Cosmos3 Nano T2V profile for SGLang-Diffusion main 3d540563.
default.notes: 4-GPU CFG parallel plus Ulysses SP for long-video H200 serving; guardrails disabled, no cache. FOUR-GPU CELLS ON THE 2026-09-13 4xB200 RUN ARE 3-4x SLOW AND IT IS NOT SGLANG. All three 4-GPU cases (this one, cosmos3 t2v 189f, cosmos3 i2v 189f) came out 3-4x slower than the SAME case and workload on H100 (07-03, 07-30) and H200 (08-26), three runs that agree with each other inside 2%. Every framework in those cells moved together -- sglang 0.25-0.32x, vLLM-Omni 0.28-0.30x, LightX2V 0.22x -- so the earlier note here calling it a suspected sglang regression was wrong, and is retracted. Nor is it the box: every 2-GPU case in that same run is 1.7-2.6x FASTER than its H200 figure. The discriminator is GPU COUNT, not model and not framework; the original investigation missed it because every image case is 2-GPU. Already eliminated, do not repeat: model unchanged since 2025-08-09, workload identical in both artifacts, warmup scales linearly, attention backend (`fa` is WORSE than the auto-selected dynamic_cudnn_sdpa), interconnect topology (NV18 all-pairs at 53.125 GB/s), offload off with 113 GiB free, MoE boundary 0.875 with both experts resident. SETTLED: a fresh 4xB200 does NOT reproduce it. MEASURED 2026-09-18 on a fresh 4xB200 (verda-b200-fin-03-3, same node family, sglang v0.5.20, cosmos3 t2v 189f, identical workload and the same `--attention-backend fa`): 2 GPU on cards 0,1 = 58.05s; 2 GPU on cards 2,3 = 58.24s; 4 GPU = 32.34s. Four-GPU scaling is healthy (1.80x over two), and the 4-GPU figure is 1.64x faster than H200's 53.09s -- the normal Blackwell gain. bench-0912 reported 214.90s for that same cell, 6.6x the healthy number. So the hardware is fine and these three cells are ARTIFACTS OF THAT BOX, not Blackwell and not sglang -- which is also the only account consistent with vLLM-Omni and LightX2V being equally slow there. Two further hypotheses died in the same experiment: `fa` is not pathological on Blackwell (arm A pins it and is 1.9x faster than H200), and the NUMA split that puts GPU3 on a different socket costs nothing measurable (58.05 vs 58.24 across it). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18 and republished: cosmos3 t2v 214.9 -> 31.7, i2v 216.0 -> 31.9, wan22 669.4 -> 106.5, each now 1.68-1.98x faster than its H200 figure, in line with every 2-GPU cell. The two cosmos3 cells ran against Cosmos3-Nano e59a53c25 rather than the 7a312c868 the rest of the artifact records -- the shared cache resolves `main` online, so the revision could not be pinned; both cells reproduce under 0.1% across two runs and vLLM-Omni moved by the same factor, so the revision does not carry the result.

default.notes: 4-GPU CFG parallel plus Ulysses SP for long-video H200 serving; guardrails disabled, no cache. Policy-aligned candidate (compile on, offload off) — NOT yet validated on H100; validate (incl. OOM risk) before publishing. FOUR-GPU CELLS ON THE 2026-09-13 4xB200 RUN ARE 3-4x SLOW AND IT IS NOT SGLANG. All three 4-GPU cases (this one, cosmos3 t2v 189f, cosmos3 i2v 189f) came out 3-4x slower than the SAME case and workload on H100 (07-03, 07-30) and H200 (08-26), three runs that agree with each other inside 2%. Every framework in those cells moved together -- sglang 0.25-0.32x, vLLM-Omni 0.28-0.30x, LightX2V 0.22x -- so the earlier note here calling it a suspected sglang regression was wrong, and is retracted. Nor is it the box: every 2-GPU case in that same run is 1.7-2.6x FASTER than its H200 figure. The discriminator is GPU COUNT, not model and not framework; the original investigation missed it because every image case is 2-GPU. Already eliminated, do not repeat: model unchanged since 2025-08-09, workload identical in both artifacts, warmup scales linearly, attention backend (`fa` is WORSE than the auto-selected dynamic_cudnn_sdpa), interconnect topology (NV18 all-pairs at 53.125 GB/s), offload off with 113 GiB free, MoE boundary 0.875 with both experts resident. SETTLED: a fresh 4xB200 does NOT reproduce it. MEASURED 2026-09-18 on a fresh 4xB200 (verda-b200-fin-03-3, same node family, sglang v0.5.20, cosmos3 t2v 189f, identical workload and the same `--attention-backend fa`): 2 GPU on cards 0,1 = 58.05s; 2 GPU on cards 2,3 = 58.24s; 4 GPU = 32.34s. Four-GPU scaling is healthy (1.80x over two), and the 4-GPU figure is 1.64x faster than H200's 53.09s -- the normal Blackwell gain. bench-0912 reported 214.90s for that same cell, 6.6x the healthy number. So the hardware is fine and these three cells are ARTIFACTS OF THAT BOX, not Blackwell and not sglang -- which is also the only account consistent with vLLM-Omni and LightX2V being equally slow there. Two further hypotheses died in the same experiment: `fa` is not pathological on Blackwell (arm A pins it and is 1.9x faster than H200), and the NUMA split that puts GPU3 on a different socket costs nothing measurable (58.05 vs 58.24 across it). RE-MEASURED 2026-09-18 and republished: cosmos3 t2v 214.9 -> 31.7, i2v 216.0 -> 31.9, wan22 669.4 -> 106.5, each now 1.68-1.98x faster than its H200 figure, in line with every 2-GPU cell. The two cosmos3 cells ran against Cosmos3-Nano e59a53c25 rather than the 7a312c868 the rest of the artifact records -- the shared cache resolves `main` online, so the revision could not be pinned; both cells reproduce under 0.1% across two runs and vLLM-Omni moved by the same factor, so the revision does not carry the result.

rtx5090-2gpu.notes: Matches docs/cookbook/diffusion/MiniMax/MiniMax-H3.mdx's verified 2xRTX5090/32GB/377GiB-host recipe as-is. The recorded numbers below (612.65s/556.79s/23366MB) were captured 2026-08-07 on minimax-h3-5090-2gpu-v4 from a run that used --dit-offload-prefetch-size 0 instead of 1, chosen at the time because prefetch-size 1 had intermittently deadlocked at 'Loading MiniMaxH3DiTModel ... Run:ai Model Streamer' on a minority of launches. That deadlock's real cause turned out to be unrelated to prefetch-size -- LayerwiseOffloadManager.__init__ clamps prefetch_size to min(max(1, prefetch_size), num_layers), so 0 and 1 are runtime-identical, and the 0-vs-1 correlation was coincidence (page-cache warmth carried over across attempts). The actual root cause: runai_model_streamer issues an unconditional torch.distributed collective (new_group + all_gather_object) inside find_local_ranks() on the first stream_files() call per component per rank, regardless of the is_distributed argument sglang passes (always False here); any per-rank divergence in layerwise-offload load order or timing can call that ad-hoc group out of lockstep and hang. Fixed at the sglang layer in sgl-project/sglang#33969 (monkeypatches find_local_ranks to skip the collective) -- serve_args here now uses the cookbook's prefetch-size 1 since 0 was never actually load-bearing; re-validate this cell once that PR lands to confirm the hang no longer reproduces even under adversarial per-rank timing. Client wall 612.65s, server-reported inference_time_s 556.79, peak_memory_mb 23366 (well under the 32 GB budget). --performance-mode speed excluded: H3's compile path changes numerics, and speed mode's residency assumption does not fit 32 GB without the layerwise knobs above. Single-GPU (num_gpus=1, tp_size=1) at this exact shape (1344x768, 124 frames) OOMs even at resident-layers=20 -- TP2's per-rank activation footprint (measured ~13 GB/rank at 100% util during a real denoise) roughly doubles unsharded on 1 GPU, on top of a 32 GB card already near its edge per the cookbook's own 2-GPU peak (~31.7 GiB/rank); the case is 2-GPU-only until that's independently reworked.

default.notes: VALIDATION PENDING (2026-10-08): derived offline from LightX2V main 0c2edc12, never run. Upstream's two-GPU MiniMax-H3 preset is configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_tp.json (the README's parallel table runs TP2 under torchrun --nproc_per_node 2), served as scripts/minimax_h3/server/start_server.sh does: --model-variant fl2av loads transformer/, there is no startup --task, and each request names task t2av. Kept from the preset: TP2 DiT, the text encoder tensor-parallel over the world group, resident DiT and text encoder, VAE spatiotemporal tile-parallel decode, sgl-kernel RMSNorm, no feature caching. Deviations from the preset, all for the benchmark's lossless policy: attn_type flash_attn3 in place of sage_attn2 (int8-QK SageAttention, a different numeric class; FA3 is the fastest exact kernel on Hopper); use_compile true (harness default) with rope_type torch_real_rope, the pairing of upstream's compile preset configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_compile.json (an eager run should go back to minimax_h3_triton_rope), but warmup false: that preset's startup warmup compiles at 480x480x158 and 544x960x124, and under torch.compile(dynamic=None) the second shape recompiles every block shape-dynamic, so the case's shape would be served by that dynamic graph -- the harness warms at the measured shape instead; use_adaln_cache false (the preset's true is required only with cpu_offload): that cache serves the ~13B-parameter, timestep-only AdaLN projections from an offline artifact built for one schedule, while sglang runs the standard path in this benchmark (its --minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path is off too), and the projections it skips are a bandwidth-bound read of about 24 GiB of weights per step, split across TP ranks (est. 0.1-0.4% of a step); infer_steps 49 (preset: 29): LightX2V counts DiT evaluations on linspace(1, 0, infer_steps + 1), sglang is sent num_inference_steps 49 (it counts forwards since sglang#38671), so both run the same 49 forwards on linspace(1, 0, 50), shifted 12 (video) / 3 (audio). size and num_frames come from each request ([768, 1344], 124). Weights: the repo's Diffusers-layout components (sglang reads the native FL2VA/ and Ref2VA/ partitions of the same repo and revision -- the same checkpoint, packaged twice by MiniMax); model_allow_patterns fetches only what LightX2V reads. vae_cpu_offload false (preset: true) on 141+ GB cards. Resident per GPU: DiT ~31 GiB + text encoder <= 31 GiB + VAEs ~10 GiB -- fits H200/B200, not an 80 GB H100. First GPU round: A/B Ulysses2 (parallel {tensor_p_size: 1, seq_p_size: 2, seq_p_attn_type: ulysses}, the topology sglang runs here) against TP2, and vae_use_compile true (compiled VAE blocks, which upstream's non-CUDA presets set) against off. Needs LightX2V >= 9ea22feb (2026-09-10, --model-variant); the installer's default pin 7efd05f8 predates H3, so a round sets LIGHTX2V_INSTALL_SPEC to main.

cases._note: vLLM-Omni requests carry extra_params.preencode_mp4=true (2026-10-08): its documented, off-by-default overlap of MP4 encoding with the VAE decode (byte-identical frames), the counterpart of sglang's default streamed encode (#41819). Both engines run their best documented output path. vLLM-Omni gets num_inference_steps 49 (2026-10-08): since vllm-omni #7219 (2026-09-24) it reads N as N model passes on linspace(1, 0, N+1), while FastVideo and TRT-LLM read 50 as 50 sigma grid points, i.e. 49 passes, and LightX2V's launch config says 49 passes; 49 gives Omni the identical 50-point grid. Earlier H3 rounds ran Omni one pass more. sglang gets num_inference_steps 49 (2026-10-23): it counts DiT forwards since sglang#38671 (2026-10-10, time_request.py: linspace(1, 0, num_steps + 1)), so the case's 50 ran 50 forwards on a 51-point grid (r1022 logs: 'infer_steps: 50', '50/50') while TRT-LLM and FastVideo read 50 as the official 50-point grid (49 forwards) and vLLM-Omni and LightX2V are given 49 forwards. 49 gives sglang the same grid.

default.notes: VALIDATION PENDING (2026-10-08): derived offline from LightX2V main 0c2edc12, never run. configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_sp.json is the four-GPU preset scripts/minimax_h3/run_minimax_h3_t2av_parallel.sh launches by default (SP4, Ulysses), served as scripts/minimax_h3/server/start_server.sh does (--model-variant fl2av, no startup --task, each request names task t2av); pure Ulysses 4 is also the topology sglang and vLLM-Omni run for this case. Kept from the preset: SP4 Ulysses, tile-parallel VAE decode, sgl-kernel RMSNorm, no feature caching. cpu_offload, text_encoder_cpu_offload and vae_cpu_offload false (preset: all true) on 141+ GB cards, and text_encoder_tensor_parallel true: the preset offloads a replicated text encoder, which resident would put up to 62 GiB more on every GPU next to the 62 GiB replicated DiT; sharding it over the world group is what upstream's SP8 configs do (minimax_h3_ref2av_sp_sol_5090.json). Deviations from the preset, all for the benchmark's lossless policy: attn_type flash_attn3 in place of sage_attn2 (int8-QK SageAttention, a different numeric class; FA3 is the fastest exact kernel on Hopper); use_compile true (harness default) with rope_type torch_real_rope, the pairing of upstream's compile preset configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_compile.json (an eager run should go back to minimax_h3_triton_rope), but warmup false: that preset's startup warmup compiles at 480x480x158 and 544x960x124, and under torch.compile(dynamic=None) the second shape recompiles every block shape-dynamic, so the case's shape would be served by that dynamic graph -- the harness warms at the measured shape instead; use_adaln_cache false (the preset's true is required only with cpu_offload): that cache serves the ~13B-parameter, timestep-only AdaLN projections from an offline artifact built for one schedule, while sglang runs the standard path in this benchmark (its --minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path is off too), and the projections it skips are a bandwidth-bound read of about 24 GiB of weights per step, split across TP ranks (est. 0.1-0.4% of a step); infer_steps 49 (preset: 29): LightX2V counts DiT evaluations on linspace(1, 0, infer_steps + 1), sglang is sent num_inference_steps 49 (it counts forwards since sglang#38671), so both run the same 49 forwards on linspace(1, 0, 50), shifted 12 (video) / 3 (audio). size and num_frames come from each request ([768, 1344], 124). Weights: the repo's Diffusers-layout components (sglang reads the native FL2VA/ and Ref2VA/ partitions of the same repo and revision -- the same checkpoint, packaged twice by MiniMax); model_allow_patterns fetches only what LightX2V reads. Resident per GPU: DiT ~62 GiB (replicated under SP) + text encoder <= 16 GiB + VAEs ~10 GiB. First GPU round: A/B TP2 x SP2 (configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_tp_sp.json: parallel {tensor_p_size: 2, seq_p_size: 2, seq_p_attn_type: ulysses}) against SP4, and vae_use_compile true against off. Needs LightX2V >= 9ea22feb (2026-09-10, --model-variant); the installer's default pin 7efd05f8 predates H3, so a round sets LIGHTX2V_INSTALL_SPEC to main.

cand-fa4-omp8.notes: Derived from `cand-fa4` (the profile B300 selects). Audit 2026-10-23 (H3 finding 1): TRT-LLM spends 5 s (2 GPU), 8 s (Ref2VA) and 11 s (4 GPU) on the CPU before its denoise loop (row_timestep_plan: torch.full, scatters and torch.unique over the whole sequence per step, on every rank) while its workers share the host's cores with OMP_NUM_THREADS unset. The harness sets OMP_NUM_THREADS for no framework; sglang caps its workers itself (min(16, cores / GPUs), gpu_worker._worker_cpu_intra_op_threads), vLLM-Omni's workers take 1 (set_multiprocessing_worker_envs) and LightX2V's torchrun sets 1, while TRT-LLM and FastVideo keep one thread per core in every worker. Combined with FA4 because this cell's sequence does not split evenly under its Ulysses size (VANILLA then runs masked SDPA; FA4 takes the trailing pad as seqused_k). VALIDATION PENDING (wave 4, 4xB300).

trtllm-visual.extra_env_reason: The harness exports PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True. Under it, the CUDA IPC handle TRT-LLM's rank 0 hands its media over with needs pidfd_getfd in the server process, which RunPod containers deny: every request logged 'pidfd_getfd: Operation not permitted' and hung to the read timeout (4xB300, 2026-10-22). Plain segments use cudaIpcMemHandle instead.

cases.prompt: The person in the reference image walks forward through a sunlit corridor, speaking to camera, footsteps and voice audible.
cases._note: Ref2VA is selected by the conditions[] entry with role=reference, not by the harness's reference_image multipart path; __TEST_IMAGE_URL__ is substituted at request time with that request's own copy of meta.test_image_url as a data: URI (until 2026-09-30 with the URL itself, which the server downloaded inside the measured window). Validated on 2x H200 2026-08-26: 222.4s single_e2e (t2va on the same box is 146.7s -- reference conditioning costs ~1.5x). The harness hands every framework the reference already at the official rule's size (reference_short_edge/reference_multiple: 2048px short edge, upscaling allowed, LANCZOS, nearest 32 -- diffusers' MiniMax-H3 modular pipeline `reference_image_short_edge`, and sglang's reference_encoding.py). vLLM-Omni stopped upscaling small references on 2026-09-28 (#8253) and ComfyUI never does, so without this they condition on ~8x fewer reference tokens than the official pipeline (the 1024x704 test image: ~2800 vs ~23800). vLLM-Omni requests carry extra_params.preencode_mp4=true (2026-10-08): its documented, off-by-default overlap of MP4 encoding with the VAE decode (byte-identical frames), the counterpart of sglang's default streamed encode (#41819). Both engines run their best documented output path. vLLM-Omni gets num_inference_steps 49 (2026-10-08): since vllm-omni #7219 (2026-09-24) it reads N as N model passes on linspace(1, 0, N+1), while FastVideo and TRT-LLM read 50 as 50 sigma grid points, i.e. 49 passes, LightX2V is configured with 49 passes, and sglang counts passes too since sglang#38671 and is sent 49 (2026-10-23); 49 gives Omni the identical 50-point grid. Earlier H3 rounds ran Omni one pass more. sglang gets num_inference_steps 49 (2026-10-23): it counts DiT forwards since sglang#38671 (2026-10-10, time_request.py: linspace(1, 0, num_steps + 1)), so the case's 50 ran 50 forwards on a 51-point grid (r1022 logs: 'infer_steps: 50', '50/50') while TRT-LLM and FastVideo read 50 as the official 50-point grid (49 forwards) and vLLM-Omni and LightX2V are given 49 forwards. 49 gives sglang the same grid.

Deviations from the preset, all for the benchmark's lossless policy: attn_type flash_attn3 in place of sage_attn2 (int8-QK SageAttention, a different numeric class; FA3 is the fastest exact kernel on Hopper); use_compile true (harness default) with rope_type torch_real_rope, the pairing of upstream's compile preset configs/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_compile.json (an eager run should go back to minimax_h3_triton_rope), but warmup false: that preset's startup warmup compiles at 480x480x158 and 544x960x124, and under torch.compile(dynamic=None) the second shape recompiles every block shape-dynamic, so the case's shape would be served by that dynamic graph -- the harness warms at the measured shape instead; use_adaln_cache false (the preset's true is required only with cpu_offload): that cache serves the ~13B-parameter, timestep-only AdaLN projections from an offline artifact built for one schedule, while sglang runs the standard path in this benchmark (its --minimax-h3-adaln-cache-path is off too), and the projections it skips are a bandwidth-bound read of about 24 GiB of weights per step, split across TP ranks (est. 0.1-0.4% of a step); infer_steps 49 (preset: 29): LightX2V counts DiT evaluations on linspace(1, 0, infer_steps + 1), sglang is sent num_inference_steps 49 (it counts forwards since sglang#38671), so both run the same 49 forwards on linspace(1, 0, 50), shifted 12 (video) / 3 (audio). size and num_frames come from each request ([768, 1344], 124). cand-fa4-omp8.notes: Derived from `cand-fa4` (the profile B300 selects). Audit 2026-10-23 (H3 finding 1): TRT-LLM spends 5 s (2 GPU), 8 s (Ref2VA) and 11 s (4 GPU) on the CPU before its denoise loop (row_timestep_plan: torch.full, scatters and torch.unique over the whole sequence per step, on every rank) while its workers share the host's cores with OMP_NUM_THREADS unset. The harness sets OMP_NUM_THREADS for no framework; sglang caps its workers itself (min(16, cores / GPUs), gpu_worker._worker_cpu_intra_op_threads), vLLM-Omni's workers take 1 (set_multiprocessing_worker_envs) and LightX2V's torchrun sets 1, while TRT-LLM and FastVideo keep one thread per core in every worker. Combined with FA4 because this cell's sequence does not split evenly under its Ulysses size (VANILLA then runs masked SDPA; FA4 takes the trailing pad as seqused_k). VALIDATION PENDING (wave 4, 4xB300).

trtllm-visual.extra_env_reason: The harness exports PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True. cases.semantics: Distilled checkpoint with trained VSA sparsity -- a lossy class under this benchmark's policy, compared as its own case because every framework serves the SAME checkpoint under the contract it declares in fastvideo_inference.json: eight DiT forwards on the rungs [999, 874, 749, 624, 500, 375, 250, 125], video/audio shift 10/3, guidance 1, 80% VSA sparsity at 64-token tiles. Not part of the lossless headline. This is the few-step, four-GPU regime where per-request fixed cost (text encode, VAE decode, MP4 encode) is a large share of latency, which the 50-step two-GPU H3 case cannot show.
cases.prompt: At night, while their owner sleeps in a bedroom, three cats march in loudly playing tiny brass instruments, then abruptly file out.
cases._note: num_inference_steps counts model evaluations (8), as vLLM-Omni does, and so does sglang since its native FastH3 V2 support (#37662: a request with 9 is rejected with 'distilled for exactly eight inference steps (nine sigma grid points, eight DiT forwards)'), so its request carries 8 -- the same eight forwards. Both engines reject any other step count or shift for this checkpoint. Both engines pin revision 71a17d72c58c (2026-09-15 14:57): the next and current revision 3da2ddfe (15:05) removed provenance.json, which vLLM-Omni's V2 loader (#7610, merged 09-17) reads to find the base-H3 VAEs, so the current revision fails there with FileNotFoundError. The weights are identical across the two revisions. guidance_scale goes to vLLM-Omni only (its recipe sends guidance_scale=1); sglang's MiniMaxH3SamplingParams fixes it at 1.0 and rejects the field in a request (400). FastVideo counts sigma grid points (its docs: `--steps` 9 is nine points and eight forwards, and its denoiser rejects any other count for this checkpoint), so its request carries 9 too; it reads the rung ladder from fastvideo_inference.json and the 10/3 shifts from the scheduler configs, both present at 71a17d72. vLLM-Omni requests carry extra_params.preencode_mp4=true (2026-10-08): its documented, off-by-default overlap of MP4 encoding with the VAE decode (byte-identical frames), the counterpart of sglang's default streamed encode (#41819). Both engines run their best documented output path.

report_framework_reasons.lightx2v: Checked 2026-10-08 against LightX2V main 0c2edc12 (2026-10-05): LightX2V cannot serve this checkpoint under its trained contract (fastvideo_inference.json). V2 is trained for VIDEO_SPARSE_ATTN_H3 at 0.8 sparsity on 64-token tiles, and LightX2V has no VSA backend (its sparse attentions -- Sparge, SVG, radial, NBHD, Sol-Attn, sparse Sage/FA4 -- are other methods; dense attention would run a different model). Its H3 scheduler builds only a uniform shifted grid from infer_steps, so the explicit rungs [999, 874, ..., 125] cannot be given (an 8-step grid starts at 1000). LightX2V's own few-step H3 paths (configs/minimax_h3/dmd/: 4- and 8-step LoRAs on the base checkpoint, mostly FP8/INT8) are a different distillation, not this checkpoint, and are not substituted.
